speaker: Unknown
en: And then I want to talk about prompt injection and red teaming, which I know is a big passion of yours, something you spend a lot of your time on.
zh: 然后我想谈谈提示词注入和红队测试，我知道这是你的一个大爱好，也是你花了很多时间在做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And let's start with just this question of, is prompt engineering a thing you need to spend your time on?
zh: 让我们先从这个问题开始，你真的需要花时间在提示工程上吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of people that, they're like, "Oh, AI is going to get really great and smart, and you don't need to actually learn these things.
zh: 有很多人，他们会说，“噢，AI 会变得非常棒、非常聪明，你不需要真正去学习这些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It'll just figure things out for you."
zh: 它会自己帮你弄明白的。”

speaker: Unknown
en: There's also this bucket of people that I imagine you're in that are like, "No, it's only becoming more important."
zh: 还有这一类人，我想你也是其中之一，他们会说，“不，它只会变得更重要。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Reid Hoffman actually just tweeted this.
zh: Reid Hoffman 实际上刚发了这条推文。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me read this tweet that he shared yesterday that supports this case.
zh: 让我读一下他昨天分享的这条支持这一观点的推文。

speaker: Unknown
en: He said, "There's this old myth that we only use 3 to 5% of our brains.
zh: 他说，“有一个古老的迷思，说我们只使用了我们大脑的 3% 到 5%。

speaker: Unknown
en: It might actually be true for how much we're getting out of AI, given our prompting skills."
zh: 考虑到我们的提示技巧，我们实际从 AI 中获取的价值可能确实只有这么多。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So what's your take on this debate?
zh: 那么你对这个辩论有什么看法？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, first of all, I think that's a great quote.
zh: 是的，首先，我认为这是一句很棒的引用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the ability to, it's called elicit certain performance improvements and behaviors from LLMs is a really big area of study.
zh: 而且，能够从 LLM 中激发出特定的性能提升和行为，是一个非常重要的研究领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: So he's absolutely right with that, but, yeah, from my perspective, prompt engineering is absolutely still here.
zh: 所以他完全是对的，但是，是的，从我的角度来看，提示工程绝对还在。

speaker: Unknown
en: I actually was at the AI Engineer World's Fair yesterday, and there was somebody, I think before me, giving a talk that prompt engineering is dead.
zh: 实际上昨天我参加了 AI Engineer World's Fair，有一个人，我想是在我之前，做了一个关于提示工程已经死了的演讲。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then my talk was next, and it was titled Prompt Engineering.
zh: 然后我的演讲紧接着就是，题目就叫 Prompt Engineering。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I was like, "Oh, I got to be prepared for that."
zh: 所以我当时就想，“噢，我得为此做好准备。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And my perspective, and this has been validated over and over again, is that people will always be saying, "It's dead," or "It's going to be dead with the next model version," but then it comes out and it's not.
zh: 我的观点，这一点已经被一次又一次地验证了，就是人们总会说，“它死了”，或者“它会在下一个模型版本中死掉”，但当新模型出来时，它并没有死。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we actually came up with a term for this, which is artificial social intelligence.
zh: 我们实际上为此想出了一个术语，叫做人工社交智能。

speaker: Unknown
en: I imagine you're familiar with the term social intelligence, describes how people communicate, interpersonal communication skills, all of that.
zh: 我想你熟悉社交智能这个术语，它描述的是人们如何交流，人际沟通技巧，所有这些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have recognized the need for a similar thing, but with communicating with AIs and understanding the best way to talk to them, understanding what their responses mean, and then how to adapt, I guess, your next prompts to that response.
zh: 我们认识到对类似东西的需求，但是是与 AI 交流，理解与它们交谈的最佳方式，理解它们的回应意味着什么，以及如何调整，我想是，你的下一个提示来回应那个回应。

speaker: Unknown
en: So over and over again, we have seen prompt engineering continue to be very important.
zh: 所以一次又一次地，我们看到提示工程继续非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's an example where changing the prompt, using some of the techniques we're going to talk about, had a big impact?
zh: 有没有这样的例子，通过改变提示，使用我们将要讨论的一些技术，产生了巨大的影响？

speaker: Unknown
en: So recently I was working on a project for a medical coding startup where we were trying to get the GenAIs, GPT‑4 in this case, to perform medical coding on a certain doctor's transcript.
zh: 所以最近我在为一个医疗编码初创公司做一个项目，我们试图让 GenAI，在这种情况下是 GPT-4，对某个医生的转录记录进行医疗编码。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I tried out all these different prompts and ways of showing the AI what it should be doing, but at the beginning of my process, I was getting little to no accuracy.
zh: 所以我尝试了所有这些不同的提示和向 AI 展示它应该做什么的方式，但在我的过程开始时，我的准确性几乎为零。

speaker: Unknown
en: It wasn't outputting the codes in a properly formatted way.
zh: 它没有以正确格式化的方式输出代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: It wasn't really thinking through well how to code the document.
zh: 它没有真正很好地思考如何对文档进行编码。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what I ended up doing was taking a long list of documents that I went and coded myself, or I guess got coded, and I took those and I attached reasonings as to why each one was coded in the way it was.
zh: 所以我最终做的是拿了一长串文档，我去自己编码了，或者我想是让人编码了，然后我把它们附上了每个编码为什么是那样编码的推理。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I took all of that data and dropped it into my prompt, and then went ahead and gave the model a new transcript it had never seen before.
zh: 然后我把所有这些数据都放到了我的提示中，然后继续给模型一个它以前从未见过的新转录记录。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that boosted the accuracy on that task up by, I think, 70%.
zh: 这将该任务的准确性提高了，我想，70%。

speaker: Unknown
en: So massive, massive performance improvements by having better prompts and doing prompt engineering well.
zh: 所以通过拥有更好的提示并做好提示工程，获得了巨大的、巨大的性能提升。

speaker: Unknown
en: Awesome.
zh: 太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm in that bucket too.
zh: 我也在那一类人里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just find there's so much value in getting better at this stuff, and the stuff we're going to talk about is not that hard to start to put some of these things in practice.
zh: 我只是发现在这方面变得更好有太多价值了，而且我们要谈论的东西并不难开始付诸实践。

speaker: Unknown
en: Another quick context question is just you have these two modes for thinking about prompt engineering.
zh: 另一个快速的背景问题是，你有这两种思考提示工程的模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think to a lot of people, they think of prompt engineering as just getting better at when you use Claude or ChatGPT, but there's actually more.
zh: 我想对很多人来说，他们认为提示工程只是在你使用 Claude 或 ChatGPT 时变得更擅长，但实际上还有更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: So talk about these two modes that you think about.
zh: 所以谈谈你思考的这两种模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this was actually a bit of a recent development for me, in terms of thinking through this and explaining it to folks.
zh: 这对我来说实际上是最近的一个发展，关于思考这个问题并向人们解释它。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the two modes are, first of all, there's the conversational mode in which most people do prompt engineering.
zh: 但这两种模式是，首先，有对话模式，大多数人在这种模式下做提示工程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is just, you're using Claude, you're using ChatGPT, you say, "Hey, can you write me this email?"
zh: 而那只是,你正在使用 Claude,你正在使用 ChatGPT,你说,"嘿,你能给我写这封邮件吗?"

speaker: Unknown
en: It does a poor job, and you're like, "Oh, no, make it more formal," or, "Add a joke in there," and it adapts its output accordingly.
zh: 它做得不好,然后你说,"噢不,让它更正式点",或者,"在那里面加个笑话",然后它相应地调整其输出。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I refer to that as conversational prompt engineering because you're getting it to improve its output over the course of a conversation.
zh: 因此我将其称为对话式提示工程,因为你在对话过程中让它改进其输出。

speaker: Unknown
en: Notably, that is not where the classical concept of prompt engineering came from.
zh: 值得注意的是,这并不是提示工程这一经典概念的来源。

speaker: Unknown
en: It actually came a bit earlier from a more, I guess, AI engineer perspective where you're like, "I have this product I'm building.
zh: 它实际上出现得稍早一点,是从一种,我猜,人工智能工程师的角度,你会说,"我正在构建这个产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have this one prompt or a couple different prompts that are super critical to this product.
zh: 我有这一个提示或几个不同的提示,它们对这个产品至关重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm running thousands, millions of inputs through this prompt each day.
zh: 我每天都要通过这个提示运行数千、数百万个输入。

speaker: Unknown
en: I need this one prompt to be perfect."
zh: 我需要这一个提示是完美的。"

speaker: Unknown
en: And so a good example of that, I guess going back to the medical coding, is I was iterating on this one single prompt.
zh: 所以我想回到医疗编码的那个好例子,就是我在迭代这一个单一的提示。
